claims.title: Independent local-flip parity attenuation and noisy cat transcript law
claims.scope: one phase-labeled ell-qubit cat block under independent identical local X-outcome flips with probability p in [0,1/2]
assumptions: the ideal local X transcript is uniform on the parity class product_i x_i=(-1)^z
local recorded outcomes are flipped independently with common probability p
nonclaims: independent identical flips are a declared model rather than a universal noise law
parity attenuation is not evidence that reality is simulated

claims.title: Proper noisy cat marginals remain phase blind
claims.scope: every proper subset of local X outcomes in the declared independently flipped cat-block model
assumptions: the complete noisy law is 2^{-ell}[1+(-1)^z(1-2p)^ell product_i y_i]
at least one physical outcome is marginalized out
nonclaims: proper-marginal blindness does not prevent the completed distributed parity transcript from carrying phase information
does not apply to arbitrary noise channels without derivation

claims.title: Exact repeated noisy-parity distinguishability bounds
claims.scope: independent repeated parity observations of one fixed binary phase through BSC(q)
assumptions: repeated preparations and readout channels are independent
the two phase hypotheses induce Bernoulli(q) and Bernoulli(1-q) parity laws
nonclaims: the KL/Pinsker count is necessary rather than sufficient
the Bhattacharyya count is sufficient rather than exact

claims.title: Noisy checkpoint weighted-Hamming geometry and sharp worst-query threshold
claims.scope: m binary checkpoint signatures whose selected final-block outcomes pass independently through one declared BSC(q)
assumptions: the future block-query distribution is exogenous and identical under compared signatures
worst-query approximation is evaluated over every allowed final-block query
nonclaims: the all-or-nothing threshold is specific to the one-step worst-query interface
internal predictive bits are not parent-hardware bits

claims.title: Exact average noisy predictive rate-distortion lower bound
claims.scope: uniform m-bit checkpoint signatures, uniform coordinate queries, and average total-variation prediction distortion D
assumptions: each target coordinate law has Bernoulli bias c Z_i with c=1-2q
the hidden signature bits are independent and uniform
the decoder may output any Bernoulli bias as a function of its finite internal state
nonclaims: different source or query distributions have different rate-distortion functions
mutual-information bits do not automatically equal physical storage energy or parent RAM

claims.title: Product-BSC codeword total variation and Bhattacharyya lower bound
claims.scope: two binary signatures at Hamming distance h observed completely through independent BSC(q) coordinates
assumptions: both compared signatures use the same crossover probability
nonclaims: the Bhattacharyya expression is a lower bound on TV rather than an equality in general
complete signature observation is different from one uniformly selected coordinate query

claims.title: Finite noisy uniform-query Gilbert predictive packing
claims.scope: m checkpoint bits under uniform final-block queries, BSC(q) reliability c=1-2q, and finite tolerance epsilon
assumptions: one renderer state determines one approximating future query law
codeword separation is measured by c times normalized Hamming distance
nonclaims: the finite Gilbert certificate is not replaced by an unsupported asymptotic count
the bound concerns a selected code family rather than all checkpoint signatures at that tolerance
